sources.title: NParks: Ocimum basilicum
sources.retrievalNote: Species-level leaf cooking and pesto description reviewed directly. Thai-basil cultivar, seed-drink and essential-oil claims were not substituted.
sources.limitation: No complete recipe quantities, cooking time or medicinal dose are provided. Food descriptions do not establish therapeutic efficacy.

sources.title: Diyaolu et al. (2021): Heavy Metals, Proximate Analysis and Brine Shrimp Lethality of Vernonia amygdalina and Ocimum gratissimum Growing in Crude Oil-Rich Delta State, Nigeria
sources.retrievalNote: Background food use and voucher identification inspected in article XML; the study concerns chemical analysis and contamination, not a cooking trial.
sources.limitation: Reported food use in Nigeria is not a verified Philippine recipe. Laboratory sample handling, brine-shrimp results and leaf oils must not become household instructions or human safety clearance.

sources.title: NParks: Ocimum tenuiflorum
sources.retrievalNote: Leaf-food paragraph and the historical synonym were read. Adjacent therapeutic tea and trial claims were not adopted.
sources.limitation: No ingredient amount, cooking duration or treatment regimen is established by the selected paragraph. Do not transfer recipes between basil species.

sources.title: NParks: Salvia rosmarinus
sources.retrievalNote: Species-level leaf-food use and the essential-oil caution reviewed, without borrowing a cultivar page's culinary wording.
sources.limitation: Leaf seasoning is not interchangeable with essential-oil ingestion or a medicinal preparation. No household recipe ratio or therapeutic dose is supplied.

sources.title: World Agroforestry, Agroforestree Database 4.0: Sesbania grandiflora
sources.retrievalNote: Unopened white-flower preparation in the Philippines was read directly. Adjacent fodder and medicinal-use paragraphs were not adopted.
sources.limitation: No cooking duration, quantity or medicinal dose is specified. Do not generalize this flower-food description to root, bark, eye-drop or other Sesbania preparations.

sources.title: World Agroforestry, Agroforestree Database 4.0: Piliostigma malabaricum
sources.retrievalNote: The leaf-condiment cooking paragraph was read separately from seed composition and medicinal-use statements.
sources.limitation: No leaf quantity, cooking time or therapeutic regimen is supplied. Food use of leaves does not clear seeds or bark for consumption.

sources.title: Medhe et al. (2022): Effect of Hydrothermal Cooking and Germination Treatment on Functional and Physicochemical Properties of Parkia timoriana Bean Flours
sources.retrievalNote: The cooking and subsequent flour-processing method was inspected directly. No numeric cooking duration is given in the reviewed subsection.
sources.limitation: Laboratory food-processing research is not a validated household recipe or human treatment. Do not substitute Parkia speciosa or Parkia biglobosa protocols.

sources.title: NParks: Nypa fruticans
sources.retrievalNote: Seed-dessert processing was read directly and corroborated on NParks' Admiralty Park page. Sap fermentation and sheath tea were not adopted.
sources.limitation: No syrup ratio, cooking duration, storage process or medicinal dose is supplied. Seed-food use does not validate other palm parts.

sources.title: NParks: Lagenaria siceraria
sources.retrievalNote: Boiling and stew descriptions were read; the page's ambiguous 'fired' wording and adjacent chest-pain syrup claim were not adopted.
sources.limitation: No food-preparation timings or clinical dose are provided. This paragraph does not address bitter-fruit or juice toxicity.

sources.title: Sharma et al. (2012): Assessment of effects on health due to consumption of bitter bottle gourd (Lagenaria siceraria) juice
sources.retrievalNote: Human adverse-event findings and the public advisory were inspected. Clinical-treatment protocols were not copied into herb advice.
sources.limitation: An adverse-event assessment, not a demonstration of medicinal benefit or a safe dose. It cannot clear bitter fruit by cooking or justify juice as treatment.

sources.title: GardeningSG: Smooth Loofah
sources.retrievalNote: Young-fruit cooking uses and the separate mature-sponge use were read directly.
sources.limitation: No cooking quantities, times or treatment instructions are supplied. Do not confuse smooth loofah with angled loofah or edible young fruit with the mature sponge.

sources.title: NParks: Luffa aegyptiaca
sources.retrievalNote: The distinction between immature vegetables, named sweet cultivars and mature inedible fruit was read directly.
sources.limitation: Do not transfer the page's raw-use statement for sweet cultivars to every plant, cultivar or mature fruit. Medicinal-use statements were not adopted.

records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: fresh or dried common-basil leaves flavour tomato dishes; fresh leaves can be blended with other ingredients into pesto. The source supplies no complete ingredient ratios, cooking duration or medicinal regimen.
reviewGaps: Do not substitute other basil species, seeds or essential-oil preparations.

records.preparationDescription: Reported food use only, not treatment: a chemical-analysis paper describes Ocimum gratissimum leaves in Nigerian soups and salads as flavouring. Its background supplies no reproducible household recipe, ingredient amount or cooking time; laboratory extracts and handling are not food instructions.
reviewGaps: Background food-use reporting is not a cooking trial or Philippine occurrence evidence.
Contaminated-site samples and brine-shrimp assays cannot establish safe human use.

records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: holy-basil leaves flavour salads and dishes containing fruit, fish or chicken. The selected food paragraph provides no ingredient amount or cooking time and does not validate a therapeutic tea regimen.
reviewGaps: Keep historical Ocimum sanctum linked to this candidate; do not borrow common-basil recipes or seed and extract doses.

records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: rosemary leaves are used as a culinary dressing or to flavour smoked or roasted meat. No ingredient ratio, cooking time or medicinal dose is supplied; leaf seasoning is not essential-oil ingestion.
reviewGaps: The source advises pregnant or breastfeeding women to avoid taking rosemary essential oil; food use does not clear medicinal oil use.

records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: the source describes unopened white flowers in the Philippines with stamen and calyx removed, then steamed or cooked in soups and stews. No amount or cooking duration is specified. This does not validate root, bark, leaf-tea or eye-drop remedies.
reviewGaps: Preserve the selected flower part and white-flowered form; do not transfer other Sesbania species' cooking methods.

records.preparationPart: Young leaves, not seeds or bark
records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: young leaves are cooked with fish or meat to flavour soup. The reviewed source provides no leaf quantity, cooking time or medicinal dose. Its separate seed-composition notes do not establish a seed-food recipe.
reviewGaps: Keep leaf-condiment use distinct from seed antinutritional substances and medicinal bark or flower infusions.

records.preparationDescription: Laboratory food-processing description, not a home recipe or treatment: a Parkia timoriana study cut and rinsed seeds, soaked them in distilled water for 12 hours and cooked them before freeze-drying and milling to flour. The reviewed subsection does not specify the numeric cooking time. No household protocol or medicinal dose is cleared.
reviewGaps: Cooking endpoint and household safety remain unresolved; freeze-drying is a laboratory operation.
Do not substitute Parkia speciosa or Parkia biglobosa processing or assume the Thai study establishes Philippine occurrence.

records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: young translucent seeds, called attap chee, are boiled in sugar syrup and added to desserts. The source specifies no syrup ratio or boiling duration. This seed-food description does not clear sap fermentation or flower-sheath tea as medicinal preparations.
reviewGaps: Preserve young-seed identity; do not substitute another palm's fruit or claim a treatment dose.

records.preparationPart: Young non-bitter fruit, not medicinal juice
records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: young bottle-gourd fruit is described as boiled or used in stews, without a specified cooking time or ingredient amount. Discard bitter fruit and do not consume bitter juice. This food description is not a medicinal juice recipe or evidence that cooking clears toxicity.
reviewGaps: The ICMR advisory warns against bitter juice; discomfort, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea after consumption requires urgent medical attention.
The human adverse-event assessment does not establish a safe medicinal dose or treatment benefit.

records.preparationPart: Immature edible fruit, not mature sponge
records.preparationDescription: Food preparation only, not treatment: young smooth-loofah fruit is fried, stewed, boiled or steamed as a vegetable. No quantity or cooking duration is given. Mature fibrous fruit is not the same food part, and a raw-use statement for sweet cultivars must not be generalized to all plants.
reviewGaps: Mature fruit is described as bitter and inedible; do not transfer angled-loofah, seed-oil or medicinal-sap instructions.

limitations: These are bounded educational preparation descriptions, not ten cleared medicinal recipes. Laboratory and reported food use remain explicitly distinguished from household instructions.
Only the stated source sections were reviewed. No new clinical efficacy assessment, local occurrence clearance, full all-state live duplicate check or publication permission is claimed.
No queue identity, image, canonical import batch, database field, UI or Dr. Ai retrieval result was changed. Earlier ledgers are preserved.
The ten rows extend preparation research to the first thirty queued candidates; the fourth and fifth batches still need preparation review. Media and all other publication gates remain separate.
